annotationRationale: All routes find the missing height and combine the two triangle areas along AC. Triangle area and segment arithmetic are shared prerequisites. Similarity, coordinate equations, and circle chord products are retained within their respective methods.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct. No repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Taking A=(0,0), C=(20,0), D=(20,30), E=(5,0) gives BD: y=2(x−5). The right-angle equation yields x=2 or 10; the intersection of the diagonal segments selects B=(2,−6). The area is 20(30+6)/2=360, matching D. No supplied figure contradicts the stem.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Independently verified and retained all three shared methods from 2020_AMC_10A_Q20: similar-triangles-and-altitude, coordinate-pythagorean-equations and diameter-circle-chord-products. They supply distinct similarity, coordinate and circle routes. Further AoPS trigonometric or alternate-altitude calculations add substantial work with little additional learner benefit.
review.annotationCheck: Composite area is an appropriate shared assessed concept, with triangle area and segment arithmetic as support. The decisive similarity, coordinate and circle tools remain explicitly mapped within their respective methods.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct. No repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The perpendicular projections establish A,F,E,C order. AA similarity gives BF=2EF. Similarity within right triangle ABC gives BF²=AF·FC, hence 4x²=(5−x)(15+x). The positive root is x=3, satisfying x<5, so BF=6 and the two areas total 360.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly reuses 2020_AMC_10A_Q20#similar-triangles-and-altitude and retains its inherited AoPS reference ID. The current AoPS Solution 1 supports the route. The altitude relation is justified rather than merely imported.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The auxiliary altitude has a clear purpose. Point order, both similarity applications, the altitude product and root selection are explained sufficiently without a diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Similarity criteria, proportional corresponding sides, quadratic factoring and composite area exactly match the derivation. The altitude product is derived from these mapped concepts and needs no additional node.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: All immediate concepts have fitting exact native-topic links. Triangle area and segment arithmetic are also correctly supplied at question level.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-SRT.B.5 applies to the similarity argument; the other supplied similarity links remain partial because transformation-based derivations and broader theorem requirements are absent. Factoring and plane-area components fit their links. Rectangle-only decomposition, solids and slope derivations are not assessed; cnm_272 has no accepted US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All immediate nodes are supported. The central altitude relation is fully derived from precise similarity nodes.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The coordinate placement respects all lengths and angles. E between B and D forces y<0 and x<5. Pythagoras gives x²−20x+y²=0; substitution factors as 5(x−2)(x−10)=0. Selecting x=2 gives height 6 and area 360.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Accurately reuses 2020_AMC_10A_Q20#coordinate-pythagorean-equations with both inherited LIVE and AoPS IDs retained. The supplied LIVE explanation and current AoPS coordinate solution support the setup. The written Pythagorean formulation is independently valid.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The axes are motivated by the perpendicular segments. Both equations, the geometric root restriction and the final area addition are explicit.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Slope, point-slope form, Pythagoras, factoring and composite area all appear directly. The squared-distance expressions follow from the mapped Pythagorean theorem, so a separate distance-formula node is unnecessary.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native links for slope, point-slope form, Pythagoras, factoring and composite area fit the written work.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The Pythagorean, quadratic-solving and plane-area components fit the supplied links. The slope links are partial: proportional-rate comparisons and similarity-based slope derivations are absent. G-GPE.B.5's parallel/perpendicular slope criteria are not established by merely writing ED's equation.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The immediate nodes accurately capture both equations and the area calculation, with no unsupported coordinate or vector technique.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Similarity gives OG=10, placing G on the diameter circle. Pythagoras gives EG=5√5. Intersecting chords give EB=75/(5√5)=3√5, and the final similarity gives BH=10·3/5=6. The opposite-side triangle areas therefore total 360.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly retains 2020_AMC_10A_Q20#diameter-circle-chord-products and its inherited AoPS ID. The candidate accurately identifies the corresponding construction as Solution 6 in the supplied current AMC 12A article. source-informed-original appropriately distinguishes project reuse from official authorship.
